components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 创 first meant a cut wound and then to create.
仓 (cāng) — near sound — 创 is chuàng; 仓 also sounds out 抢 qiǎng and 枪 qiāng.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 造 is to go and make something.
告 (gào) is a loose sound clue (-ao); also in 浩 hào, 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 他们创造了一个新的记录。
example.pinyin: Tāmen chuàngzào le yí gè xīn de jìlù.
example.english: They created a new record.
example.fact: 创造 emphasizes bringing something genuinely new into existence — an invention, a record, a work of art — while its near-synonym 制造 ("to manufacture") is reserved for producing something already known, like a factory turning out identical products; mixing the two up is a common learner slip.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢创造新的游戏。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan chuàngzào xīn de yóuxì.
examples.english: Kids like creating new games.

examples.hanzi: 好的老师能为学生创造学习机会。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo de lǎoshī néng wèi xuésheng chuàngzào xuéxí jīhuì.
examples.english: Good teachers can create learning opportunities for students.

components.note: 今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn hǎo.
example.english: The weather is very nice today.
example.fact: 今 is a bound morpheme in time words: 今天 (today), 今年 (this year), 今晚 (tonight), 今后 (from now on). On its own it is classical: 古今 means ancient and modern.

examples.hanzi: 今年的冬天比往年冷。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de dōngtiān bǐ wǎngnián lěng.
examples.english: This winter is colder than previous years.

examples.hanzi: 他至今没有结婚。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhìjīn méiyǒu jiéhūn.
examples.english: He has not married to this day.

components.note: 乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.

example.hanzi: 凶手杀害了三名受害者。
example.pinyin: Xiōngshǒu shāhài le sān míng shòuhàizhě.
example.english: The murderer killed three victims.
example.fact: 杀害 is the formal, written-register word for unlawful killing used in news and legal contexts — plain 杀 alone is more neutral and can describe killing in general, including animals or killing in fiction and games, while 杀害 specifically frames the act as a crime against a person.

examples.hanzi: 这起案件中,有两个人被杀害了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ ànjiàn zhōng, yǒu liǎng ge rén bèi shāhài le.
examples.english: In this case, two people were murdered.

examples.hanzi: 那位老人被坏人杀害了。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi lǎorén bèi huàirén shāhài le.
examples.english: That old man was murdered by bad people.

components.note: 内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 她表面平静,内心却很紧张。
example.pinyin: Tā biǎomiàn píngjìng, nèixīn què hěn jǐnzhāng.
example.english: She looked calm on the outside, but inside she was very nervous.
example.fact: 内心 stacks "inside" (内) directly onto "heart" (心) to name one's inner emotional world, often set up in deliberate contrast with 表面 ("surface, outward appearance") — the pattern 表面...内心却... ("outwardly... but inwardly...") is a common way to describe a gap between how someone looks and how they actually feel.

examples.hanzi: 在内心深处,他还是爱着她。
examples.pinyin: Zài nèixīn shēnchù, tā háishi ài zhe tā.
examples.english: Deep down, he still loves her.

examples.hanzi: 我的内心很平静,一点儿也不紧张。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de nèixīn hěn píngjìng, yìdiǎnr yě bù jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: My heart is calm and not nervous at all.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 日 is the sun — 暴 originally meant to expose to the sun (still in 暴露), then violent, as in 暴力.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 电视上有太多暴力的画面。
example.pinyin: Diànshì shàng yǒu tài duō bàolì de huàmiàn.
example.english: There's too much violent imagery on TV.
example.fact: 暴 alone already means "sudden, violent, fierce," as in 暴雨 ("violent rainstorm") and 暴风 ("violent windstorm") — 暴力 narrows that general sense specifically to violence done to people, adding 力 ("force") to make the meaning concrete and physical.

examples.hanzi: 暴力解决不了任何问题。
examples.pinyin: Bàolì jiějué bù liǎo rènhé wèntí.
examples.english: Violence solves no problems.

examples.hanzi: 孩子不应该看暴力的电影。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bù yīnggāi kàn bàolì de diànyǐng.
examples.english: Children shouldn't watch violent movies.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; 脏 is an organ (zàng), and also dirty (zāng).
庄 (zhuāng) is a near sound match for zàng/zāng; also in 装 zhuāng.

example.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒu tài zāng le.
example.english: Your hands are too dirty.
example.fact: Simplified 脏 merges two old characters, 髒 (zāng, dirty) and 臟 (zàng, organs). So the same shape reads zāng in 肮脏 (filthy) but zàng in 心脏 (heart) and 内脏 (internal organs).

examples.hanzi: 他的衣服太脏了，该洗了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yīfu tài zāng le, gāi xǐ le.
examples.english: His clothes are too dirty and need washing.

examples.hanzi: 别说脏话。
examples.pinyin: Bié shuō zānghuà.
examples.english: Don't use foul language.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.pinyin: Tā shēngqì de shuō: “Nǐ zǒukāi!”
example.english: He said angrily, "Go away!"
example.fact: 走开 as a bare command (走开!, "go away!") sounds sharp and even rude in Mandarin — for a neutral, polite way to ask someone to move aside, speakers reach instead for 让一下 or 借过, so 走开 is one to use carefully depending on tone and relationship.

examples.hanzi: 这里是我的座位,请你走开。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ shì wǒ de zuòwèi, qǐng nǐ zǒukāi.
examples.english: This is my seat, please move away.

examples.hanzi: 那只狗在我身边不肯走开。
examples.pinyin: Nà zhī gǒu zài wǒ shēnbiān bù kěn zǒukāi.
examples.english: That dog won't walk away from my side.

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
古 (gǔ) is a close sound clue for gù; 古 also in 姑 gū and 固 gù.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: an action with a cause.

example.hanzi: 昨天路上发生了一起交通事故。
example.pinyin: Zuótiān lù shàng fāshēng le yì qǐ jiāotōng shìgù.
example.english: A traffic accident happened on the road yesterday.
example.fact: 事故 pairs the general 事 ("matter, affair") with 故 ("cause, reason") to name an unplanned "incident with a cause." It's reserved for something unfortunate and usually unintentional (交通事故, "traffic accident"), unlike the neutral 事情 ("matter, affair"), which carries no accident or mishap connotation at all.

examples.hanzi: 这次事故没有人受伤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shìgù méiyǒu rén shòushāng.
examples.english: Nobody was hurt in this accident.

examples.hanzi: 因为一个小事故,路上堵了一个小时。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi yí ge xiǎo shìgù, lù shang dǔ le yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: Because of a minor accident, the road was jammed for an hour.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — 艺 originally meant planting and cultivating, later skill and art.
乙 (yǐ) — near sound — 艺 is yì, same syllable with another tone.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.

example.pinyin: Tā duì yìshù hěn gǎn xìngqù.
example.english: She's very interested in art.
example.fact: 术 on its own means "technique, skill, method," as in 技术 ("technology/skill") and 手术 ("surgery") — 艺术 builds "art" by combining it with 艺 ("skill, craft"), framing art at its root as a cultivated technical skill rather than pure inspiration, a rather different emphasis from the Western Romantic idea of the unteachable "artistic genius."

examples.hanzi: 这座城市有很多艺术博物馆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu hěn duō yìshù bówùguǎn.
examples.english: This city has many art museums.

examples.hanzi: 他想成为一名艺术家,所以学习艺术。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chéngwéi yì míng yìshùjiā, suǒyǐ xuéxí yìshù.
examples.english: He wants to become an artist, so he studies art.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 满 is filled with water, full.
The right half is a short form of 㒼 (mǎn), the sound part, also in 瞒 mán.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.pinyin: Gùkè duì fúwù hěn mǎnyì.
example.english: The customer is very satisfied with the service.
example.fact: 满 alone means "full" — a cup filled to the brim — and 意 means "intention, wish" — 满意 combines them into something not unlike "one's wishes fully met," an image close to the English idiom of one's "cup being full" when deeply satisfied.

examples.hanzi: 这个结果你满意吗?
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiéguǒ nǐ mǎnyì ma?
examples.english: Are you satisfied with this result?

examples.hanzi: 老板对他的工作很满意。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn duì tā de gōngzuò hěn mǎnyì.
examples.english: The boss is very satisfied with his work.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.

example.hanzi: 大多数学生都同意这个看法。
example.pinyin: Dàduōshù xuésheng dōu tóngyì zhège kànfǎ.
example.english: The majority of students agree with this view.
example.fact: 大多数 tacks the intensifier 大 ("big, great") onto 多数 ("the greater number, majority") for emphasis — 多数 alone already means "majority," so 大多数 leans closer to "the overwhelming majority," even though both are usually translated into English simply as "most."

examples.hanzi: 大多数人都喜欢周末。
examples.pinyin: Dà duōshù rén dōu xǐhuan zhōumò.
examples.english: Most people like weekends.

examples.hanzi: 我们班大多数同学都会游泳。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān dà duōshù tóngxué dōu huì yóuyǒng.
examples.english: Most of the students in our class can swim.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving — 速 is speed, as in 快速 and 速度.
束 (shù) — near sound — 速 is sù, same syllable with different initial.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē de sùdù tài kuài le.
example.english: This car's speed is too fast.
example.fact: 度 by itself already means "a measured degree," as in 温度 ("temperature," literally "warmth degree") — 速度 builds "speed" as literally "the degree of quickness," the same measuring logic behind 湿度 ("humidity") and 高度 ("height, altitude"), a whole family of X度 words naming a quantified degree of X.

examples.hanzi: 请把速度放慢一点儿。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ sùdù fàng màn yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: Please slow down a bit.

examples.hanzi: 网络速度太慢了,视频一直卡住。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngluò sùdù tài màn le, shìpín yìzhí kǎ zhù.
examples.english: The internet is too slow and the video keeps freezing.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.

example.pinyin: Tā de shénjīng hěn jǐnzhāng.
example.english: His nerves are very tense.
example.fact: Beyond its anatomical sense, 神经 doubles as an informal insult — calling someone 神经 or 神经病 suggests they're acting unhinged or crazy, similar to how English can call an erratic person "a basket case," extending a medical term into casual slang about someone's mental state.

examples.hanzi: 他的手指神经受了伤。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒuzhǐ shénjīng shòu le shāng.
examples.english: The nerves in his finger were injured.

examples.hanzi: 你是不是神经有问题?别这样说话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì shénjīng yǒu wèntí? Bié zhèyàng shuōhuà.
examples.english: Are you out of your mind? Don't talk like that.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 三点水 marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 酒 liquor, 河 river; 汤 is soup or hot water.
昜 (yáng) — near sound — 汤 is tāng; 昜 also sounds out 扬 yáng, 场 chǎng, 烫 tàng.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women and female roles, as in 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 姑 aunt; 姆 is a nanny, as in 保姆.
母 (mǔ) — same sound — 姆 is mǔ, just like 母 (mother).

example.pinyin: Tāngmǔ shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: Tom is my friend.
example.fact: 汤姆 is a phonetic transliteration built purely for sound, not sense — 汤 ("soup") and 姆 (a term for a female caretaker, as in 保姆, "nanny") contribute nothing to the meaning "Tom." Both characters are chosen only because their pronunciations, tāng and mǔ, approximate the English name.

examples.hanzi: 汤姆今天没来上课。
examples.pinyin: Tāngmǔ jīntiān méi lái shàngkè.
examples.english: Tom didn't come to class today.

examples.hanzi: 你认识汤姆吗?他是我的邻居。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Tāngmǔ ma? Tā shì wǒ de línjū.
examples.english: Do you know Tom? He's my neighbor.

components.note: 牛 (ox, cattle) — 牛 marks cattle and animals, as in 牲, 物, 特; 牺 was a pure sacrificial ox.
西 (xī) — same sound — 牺 is xī, like 西 west.
牛 (ox, cattle) — 牛 for cattle and livestock, as in 牺, 物, 特; 牲 is a sacrificial or domestic animal.
生 (shēng) — same sound — 牲 is shēng, like 生; the pair 牺牲 means sacrifice.

example.hanzi: 他为了家人牺牲了自己的事业。
example.pinyin: Tā wèile jiārén xīshēng le zìjǐ de shìyè.
example.english: He sacrificed his own career for his family.
example.fact: 牺牲 originally named the livestock, typically oxen (hence 牛 in both characters), slaughtered in ancient ritual offerings to gods or ancestors — the modern, everyday sense of "to give something up for a greater cause" is a metaphorical extension of that literal ritual sacrifice.

examples.hanzi: 父母为孩子牺牲了很多。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ wèi háizi xīshēng le hěn duō.
examples.english: Parents sacrifice a lot for their children.

examples.hanzi: 这位战士牺牲得很光荣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zhànshì xīshēng de hěn guāngróng.
examples.english: This soldier gave his life with honor.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 力 marks strength and effort, as in 办, 动, 努, 助; 勇 is strength in action, courage.
甬 (yǒng) — same sound — 勇 is yǒng, like 甬; 甬 also sounds out 通 tōng, 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng.
攵 (tap) — the right part and radical, a hand with a stick, as in 收. Dictionary story: striking a beast, which takes courage, hence 勇敢 brave.
耳 (ear) — the left part, said to stand for a beast. Memory aid: dare to grab a beast by the ear.

example.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán fēicháng yǒnggǎn.
example.english: Firefighters are extremely brave.
example.fact: 敢 alone already means "to dare" (敢不敢, "dare you or not") — its traditional graphic story shows a hand with a stick confronting a wild beast, a fitting root image for the boldness in the face of danger that 勇敢 names.

examples.hanzi: 你真勇敢,敢一个人去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhēn yǒnggǎn, gǎn yí ge rén qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: You're so brave, daring to travel alone.

examples.hanzi: 面对困难,我们要勇敢一些。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì kùnnan, wǒmen yào yǒnggǎn yìxiē.
examples.english: In the face of difficulties, we need to be a bit braver.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 忄 is the heart radical for emotions, as in 怕, 情, 慌; 愤 is anger and resentment.
贲 (bēn) — near sound — 愤 is fèn; 贲 also sounds out 喷 pēn.
心 (heart) — 心 marks emotions and thought, as in 想, 思, 急; 怒 is rage.
奴 (nú) — same sound, different tone — 怒 is nù; 奴 also sounds out 努 nǔ.

example.hanzi: 他的愤怒完全无法控制。
example.pinyin: Tā de fènnù wánquán wúfǎ kòngzhì.
example.english: His anger was completely uncontrollable.
example.fact: 愤怒 sits at the intense, literary end of Mandarin's anger vocabulary — closer to "wrath, fury" than the everyday, conversational 生气 ("to get angry, annoyed") — so it shows up far more often in writing, news, or formal speech than in casual chat.

examples.hanzi: 听到这件事,他非常愤怒。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhè jiàn shì, tā fēicháng fènnù.
examples.english: He was furious when he heard about it.

examples.hanzi: 人们愤怒地离开了会场。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen fènnù de líkāi le huìchǎng.
examples.english: The people angrily left the meeting hall.

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié hěn hé jiǎo.
example.english: These shoes fit well.
example.fact: 合 is about things fitting together: 合适 (suitable), 合作 (to cooperate), 合同 (contract), 合影 (group photo). As a verb it also means to close, as in 合上书 (close the book).

examples.hanzi: 他合上书，准备睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé shàng shū, zhǔnbèi shuìjiào.
examples.english: He closed the book and got ready for bed.

examples.hanzi: 这个价格很合理。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiàgé hěn hélǐ.
examples.english: This price is quite reasonable.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
子 (child) — a child in a house: to bear and nurture; characters were later "born" from other characters.

example.hanzi: 这份报告里有很多数字。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào lǐ yǒu hěn duō shùzì.
example.english: This report contains a lot of figures.
example.fact: 数字 covers both "a numeral" (a single digit) and, as an adjective, "digital" (数字相机, "digital camera") — the same two characters doing double duty for "number" and "digital" mirrors how English also repurposed "digital" from "relating to digits" into "computerized."

examples.hanzi: 请在这里写下你的电话数字。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ xiěxià nǐ de diànhuà shùzì.
examples.english: Please write down your phone number here.

examples.hanzi: 这个数字代表什么意思?
examples.pinyin: Zhège shùzì dàibiǎo shénme yìsi?
examples.english: What does this number mean?

components.note: 奇 (qí) is a sound clue for 骑 qí, 寄 jì, 椅 yǐ and 崎 qí; as a word it means strange or remarkable.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhēn shì yí jiàn qíguài de shì.
example.english: This is really a strange thing.
example.fact: 奇 has two readings: qí (strange: 好奇 curious, 奇迹 miracle) and jī (odd, as in 奇数, an odd number, opposite of 偶数). 奇怪 is the common spoken word for "strange".

examples.hanzi: 这里的风景真奇妙。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng zhēn qímiào.
examples.english: The scenery here is truly wonderful.

examples.hanzi: 他是个很奇怪的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè hěn qíguài de rén.
examples.english: He is a very strange person.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a cat's meow; also in 叫 shout, 喵 meow.
米 (mǐ) gives the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 眯 mī.

example.hanzi: 我家有一只可爱的猫咪。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī kě'ài de māomī.
example.english: We have a cute kitten at home.
example.fact: 咪 imitates the sound of a cat and is nearly always seen in 猫咪, an affectionate word for a pet cat. Calling a cat is 咪咪 (mīmī). Don't confuse it with 眯 (mī, to squint).

examples.hanzi: 猫咪在沙发上睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Māomī zài shāfā shang shuìjiào.
examples.english: The kitty is sleeping on the sofa.

examples.hanzi: 你家的猫咪叫什么名字？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā de māomī jiào shénme míngzi?
examples.english: What's your kitty's name?

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 (silk thread); early paper was made from silk and fibres, so 纸 sits with 红, 线, 给.
氏 (shì) — only a loose sound hint today — 纸 is zhǐ while 氏 is shì.

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhāng zhǐ.
example.english: Please give me a sheet of paper.
example.fact: Paper (造纸术) is one of China's Four Great Inventions, traditionally credited to the court official 蔡伦 around AD 105, though older paper has been found. The measure word is 张: 一张纸. 报纸 is a newspaper.

examples.hanzi: 我想写一张纸条给他。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiě yì zhāng zhǐtiáo gěi tā.
examples.english: I want to write him a note.

examples.hanzi: 这张纸太薄了，写字会透。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhǐ tài báo le, xiězì huì tòu.
examples.english: This paper is too thin; the writing will show through.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.pinyin: Yàoshi diào zài dìshang le.
example.english: The keys fell on the ground.
example.fact: 地上 pairs 地 ("earth, ground") with the light, neutral-toned suffix 上 ("on top of") to mean "on the ground/floor" — the same suffix pattern appears in 桌子上 ("on the table") and 床上 ("on the bed"), one of Mandarin's most productive ways to build a location phrase out of any noun.

examples.hanzi: 地上有水,小心别滑倒。
examples.pinyin: Dì shang yǒu shuǐ, xiǎoxīn bié huá dǎo.
examples.english: There's water on the floor, be careful not to slip.

examples.hanzi: 小狗躺在地上睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu tǎng zài dì shang shuìjiào.
examples.english: The puppy is sleeping on the ground.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants; 范 was originally a plant name, and later pattern or model, as in 范围 scope.
氾 (fàn) — same sound — 范 is fàn, like 氾.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 图; 围 is to surround.
韦 (wéi) sounds exactly like 围; also in 违 wéi and 伟 wěi.

example.hanzi: 这个问题超出了我的知识范围。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí chāochū le wǒ de zhīshi fànwéi.
example.english: This question is beyond the scope of my knowledge.
example.fact: 围 traces back to 囗, a picture of an enclosure hemming something in on every side; 范围 extends that physical boundary image metaphorically from enclosed space to abstract scope, as in 超出范围 ("beyond the scope") — the same figurative move English makes when it calls an idea's limits its "boundaries."

examples.hanzi: 这个活动的范围很广。
examples.pinyin: Zhège huódòng de fànwéi hěn guǎng.
examples.english: The scope of this event is very wide.

examples.hanzi: 请在规定的范围内选择。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài guīdìng de fànwéi nèi xuǎnzé.
examples.english: Please choose within the specified range.

components.note: 尺 (chǐ, ruler) — the visible top part, as in 尺寸 size. 尽 simplifies 盡 and the shape does not explain 'use up'. Memory aid: measure it to the very end.
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.pinyin: Wǒ huì jǐnliàng zǎo diǎn dào.
example.english: I'll try to arrive as early as possible.
example.fact: 尽量 is easy to confuse with the similarly-spelled 尽力 ("to put in one's full effort/strength"): 尽量 specifically means doing something to the greatest possible extent or quantity (尽量多, "as much as possible"), while 尽力 is about maximum effort, not necessarily maximum amount.

examples.hanzi: 你尽量不要熬夜。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jǐnliàng bú yào áoyè.
examples.english: Try not to stay up late as much as you can.

examples.hanzi: 他尽量帮我们解决问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǐnliàng bāng wǒmen jiějué wèntí.
examples.english: He tried his best to help us solve the problem.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — marks grain and crops, as in 秋, 种, 租; 称 originally meant weighing grain, then naming (称呼).

example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu chēng tā wéi Lǎo Wáng.
example.english: Everyone calls him Old Wang.
example.fact: 称 is chēng in 称呼 (form of address), 称赞 (to praise) and 称为 (to be called). It is chèn in 相称 (to match) and 称心 (satisfying), a different word with the same character.

examples.hanzi: 大家都称他为"老师"。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu chēng tā wéi "lǎoshī".
examples.english: Everyone calls him "teacher".

examples.hanzi: 我们去称一下这个西瓜有多重。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù chēng yíxià zhège xīguā yǒu duō zhòng.
examples.english: Let's weigh this watermelon to see how heavy it is.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骗, 驾, 验; 骑 is to ride.
奇 (qí) — same sound — 骑 is qí, like 奇; 奇 also sounds out 椅 yǐ.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
example.english: I ride my bike to work every day.
example.fact: 骑 is the verb for straddled mounts: 骑马, 骑车, 骑摩托车. For cars and trains Chinese uses 坐 (ride as a passenger) or 开 (drive), so 骑 depends on how you sit.

examples.hanzi: 孩子喜欢骑马。
examples.pinyin: Háizi xǐhuan qí mǎ.
examples.english: The child likes riding horses.

examples.hanzi: 他骑车上班要半个小时。
examples.pinyin: Tā qí chē shàngbān yào bàn gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: It takes him half an hour to cycle to work.

components.note: 大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.
阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阴, 院, 队; 阳 is the sunny side of a hill, with 日 sun.
日 (sun) — 日 is the sun, as in 明, 晴, 时.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān de tàiyang hěn dà.
example.english: The sun is really strong today.
example.fact: 阳 names the sunlit side of a hill or place (阝 "hillside" + 日 "sun") and is also half of the yīn-yáng (阴阳) pair representing shade and light. 太阳 tacks on 太 ("very, extremely") for emphasis — literally something like "the extremely bright one."

examples.hanzi: 太阳从东边升起来了。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyang cóng dōngbian shēng qǐlái le.
examples.english: The sun has risen in the east.

examples.hanzi: 别在太阳底下待太久。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài tàiyang dǐxia dāi tài jiǔ.
examples.english: Don't stay out in the sun for too long.

components.note: 午 (noon) — an old picture of a pestle or mallet, later borrowed for 'noon'. Memory aid: noon is when the sun stands straight overhead — 下午, 午饭.
食 (food) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱 (as 饣); 餐 is a meal.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǔcān ba.
example.english: Let's have lunch together.
example.fact: 午餐 is the more formal, written-register word for "lunch" — everyday spoken Mandarin reaches far more often for 午饭 (also in this batch), built from the plainer 饭 ("cooked rice, meal"), while 餐 (from 食, "food") carries a slightly more refined tone, as in 早餐/午餐/晚餐 versus the everyday 早饭/午饭/晚饭.

examples.hanzi: 今天的午餐是米饭和青菜。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de wǔcān shì mǐfàn hé qīngcài.
examples.english: Today's lunch is rice and vegetables.

examples.hanzi: 公司为员工提供免费午餐。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī wèi yuángōng tígōng miǎnfèi wǔcān.
examples.english: The company provides free lunch for its employees.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 他在会议上提出了一个新想法。
example.pinyin: Tā zài huìyì shàng tíchū le yí gè xīn xiǎngfǎ.
example.english: He raised a new idea at the meeting.
example.fact: 提出 combines 提 ("to lift, to carry") with the directional complement 出 ("out") to mean literally "to lift out" — a "lift into view" image close to what English does with its own "to raise" a question or proposal, one of the cases where the two languages' metaphors happen to line up.

examples.hanzi: 我想向大家提出一个问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiàng dàjiā tíchū yí ge wèntí.
examples.english: I'd like to raise a question to everyone.

examples.hanzi: 她提出要搬到城里去住。
examples.pinyin: Tā tíchū yào bān dào chéng lǐ qù zhù.
examples.english: She proposed moving to live in the city.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 日 stands for day and time, as in 时, 晚, 早; 暂 is "for a short time".
斩 (zhǎn) — near sound — 暂 is zàn; 斩 also sounds out 渐 jiàn and 惭 cán.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì zànshí de kùnnan.
example.english: This is only a temporary difficulty.
example.fact: 暂时 works as both an adjective ("temporary") and, more commonly, an adverb meaning "for now, for the time being" placed right before a verb (暂时不能, "can't for now") — English needs two different phrases for these two uses, where Mandarin reuses the same word.

examples.hanzi: 我暂时不想换工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zànshí bù xiǎng huàn gōngzuò.
examples.english: I don't want to change jobs for now.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法只能暂时用一下。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ zhǐ néng zànshí yòng yíxià.
examples.english: This method can only be used temporarily.

components.note: 午 (noon) — an old picture of a pestle or mallet, later borrowed for 'noon'. Memory aid: noon is when the sun stands straight overhead — 下午, 午饭.
饣 (food, simplified 食) — meals and eating: 饿 hungry, 饱 full, 饺 dumpling; 饭 is cooked rice or a meal.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match for fàn; also in 板 bǎn.

example.pinyin: Nǐ wǔfàn chī le shénme?
example.english: What did you have for lunch?
example.fact: 饭 (from 饣 "food" + the sound component 反) literally means "cooked rice" before broadening to "meal" in general — the same shift 饭 makes in 吃饭 ("to eat," literally "to eat rice"), where the specific staple food came to stand for the whole act of eating.

examples.hanzi: 午饭后我们去公园走走吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǔfàn hòu wǒmen qù gōngyuán zǒuzou ba.
examples.english: Let's take a walk in the park after lunch.

examples.hanzi: 他每天都自己带午饭。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān dōu zìjǐ dài wǔfàn.
examples.english: He brings his own lunch every day.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to grip or rely on.
居 (jū) is a close sound clue for jù; 居 also in 剧 jù and 锯 jù.

example.pinyin: Jùshuō míngtiān huì xià yǔ.
example.english: It is said that it will rain tomorrow.
example.fact: 据 is a bound morpheme in 根据 (according to), 数据 (data), 证据 (evidence), 据说 (it is said) and 据点 (stronghold). 据 is the written form of "according to"; the spoken equivalent is 按照.

examples.hanzi: 据报道，明天会下大雪。
examples.pinyin: Jù bàodào, míngtiān huì xià dàxuě.
examples.english: According to reports, it will snow heavily tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 他的话没有根据。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà méiyǒu gēnjù.
examples.english: What he said has no basis.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 优 first meant a person who performs or is excellent, in 演员 and 优秀.
尤 (yóu) — near sound — 优 is yōu; 尤 also sounds out 忧 yōu.
禾 (grain) — 禾 is the grain plant, as in 种, 秋; 秀 first meant a plant coming into flower or ear, then graceful and outstanding.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng yōuxiù de lǎoshī.
example.english: She is an outstanding teacher.
example.fact: 秀 alone already means "to flower, to bloom," describing a grain crop coming into flower, and by extension "to excel, to stand out" — 优秀 pairs it with 优 ("superior, excellent") to describe a person or thing that has, so to speak, come into full bloom.

examples.hanzi: 他在班上的成绩很优秀。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bān shang de chéngjì hěn yōuxiù.
examples.english: His grades in class are outstanding.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章写得非常优秀。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng xiě de fēicháng yōuxiù.
examples.english: This article is very well written.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).

example.pinyin: Jīnglǐ qīnzì lái dàoqiàn le.
example.english: The manager came to apologize in person.
example.fact: 亲自 emphasizes that someone did something themselves rather than delegating it (亲自来, "came in person," rather than sending someone else) — it pairs the "closeness, intimacy" sense of 亲 with the reflexive 自 ("self"), underscoring direct, hands-on involvement.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我想亲自去看看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ xiǎng qīnzì qù kànkan.
examples.english: I want to go and see this matter in person.

examples.hanzi: 她亲自给每个客人倒了茶。
examples.pinyin: Tā qīnzì gěi měi ge kèrén dào le chá.
examples.english: She poured tea for each guest herself.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth, as in 吹 blow, 欢 joyful; 歌 is the mouth opened in song.
哥 (gē) — same sound — 歌 is gē, just like 哥; 哥 means elder brother.
曲 (bent) — the shape pictures something bent; qū means crooked and qǔ means a song, as in 歌曲.

example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gēqǔ hěn hǎotīng.
example.english: This song sounds really nice.
example.fact: 歌 and 曲 are near-synonyms doubled into one word: 歌 emphasizes the sung lyrics (from 欠, a mouth exhaling breath) while 曲 emphasizes the melody or tune, so 歌曲 covers a song as a whole, words and music together — and it takes the measure word 首, as in 一首歌曲.

examples.hanzi: 她唱了一首很美的歌曲。
examples.pinyin: Tā chàng le yì shǒu hěn měi de gēqǔ.
examples.english: She sang a very beautiful song.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌曲是我最喜欢的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gēqǔ shì wǒ zuì xǐhuan de.
examples.english: This song is my favorite.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 迟 is slow going, late.
尺 (chǐ) is a close sound match, tone differs.

example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ chídào le.
example.english: Sorry, I'm late.
example.fact: 迟 means late past an expected time: 迟到 (to arrive late), 迟早 (sooner or later), 推迟 (to postpone). 晚 is just late in the day or after a time, whereas 迟 implies a missed deadline.

examples.hanzi: 火车晚点了，我们可能会迟到。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē wǎndiǎn le, wǒmen kěnéng huì chídào.
examples.english: The train is late and we may be late too.

examples.hanzi: 你怎么来得这么迟？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme lái de zhème chí?
examples.english: Why have you come so late?

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women and family terms, as in 妈, 姐, 姑; 婴 is an infant, as in 婴儿.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.pinyin: Nàge yīngér gāng chūshēng sān tiān.
example.english: That baby was born just three days ago.
example.fact: 婴 (built around 女 "woman," evoking the mother) and 儿 (a pictograph of a small child, drawn with an oversized head) combine into the formal, written-register word for "infant" — everyday spoken Mandarin reaches instead for the plainer, more affectionate 宝宝 ("baby") far more often than 婴儿.

examples.hanzi: 这个婴儿哭了一整晚。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yīng'ér kū le yì zhěng wǎn.
examples.english: This baby cried all night.

examples.hanzi: 婴儿需要很多睡眠。
examples.pinyin: Yīng'ér xūyào hěn duō shuìmián.
examples.english: Babies need a lot of sleep.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌: 极 first meant a roof beam, the very top.
及 (jí) gives the exact sound; also in 级 jí and 吸 xī.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì jí hǎo.
example.english: The weather is extremely good today.
example.fact: 极 works as an adverb before an adjective (极好) or after one with 了: 好极了 (just great!). It also means a geographic or electrical pole: 南极, 北极, 阴极. 积极 (positive, active) and 极端 (extreme) are common compounds.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子聪明极了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi cōngmíng jí le.
examples.english: This child is extremely smart.

examples.hanzi: 北极的冬天非常冷。
examples.pinyin: Běijí de dōngtiān fēicháng lěng.
examples.english: Winter in the Arctic is extremely cold.

components.note: 夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 他讲的笑话把大家逗笑了。
example.pinyin: Tā jiǎng de xiàohua bǎ dàjiā dòuxiào le.
example.english: The joke he told made everyone laugh.
example.fact: 笑话 works as both a noun ("a joke") and a verb ("to mock, laugh at") without any change in form — 讲笑话 means "to tell a joke," while 别笑话我 means "don't make fun of me," the same two characters serving opposite grammatical roles.

examples.hanzi: 你别拿我的名字开笑话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié ná wǒ de míngzi kāi xiàohua.
examples.english: Don't make a joke out of my name.

examples.hanzi: 她怕别人笑话她的口音。
examples.pinyin: Tā pà biérén xiàohua tā de kǒuyīn.
examples.english: She's afraid that others will laugh at her accent.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
忄 (heart) — 忄 is the heart radical for feelings, as in 情, 怕; 惜 is the feeling of cherishing.
昔 (xī) — same sound — 惜 is xī, like 昔 (in the past); 昔 also sounds out 借 jiè and 错 cuò.

example.hanzi: 可惜我们没赶上那场演出。
example.pinyin: Kěxī wǒmen méi gǎnshàng nà chǎng yǎnchū.
example.english: It's a pity we didn't catch that show.
example.fact: 可惜 usually opens a sentence as a stand-alone comment on a regrettable fact, much like English "unfortunately" — but it can also sit inside a sentence as a predicate ("这可惜了", "what a shame"), giving it more flexibility than a fixed sentence adverb.

examples.hanzi: 这么好的机会,没抓住真可惜。
examples.pinyin: Zhème hǎo de jīhuì, méi zhuā zhù zhēn kěxī.
examples.english: Such a good chance, and it's a pity not to have taken it.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服太可惜了,洗坏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài kěxī le, xǐ huài le.
examples.english: It's such a shame about this shirt, it got ruined in the wash.

components.note: 兰 (orchid) — simplified from 蘭, which had the grass radical 艹 on top and 闌 giving the sound lán — a plant name.

example.hanzi: 她在窗台上养了一盆兰花。
example.pinyin: Tā zài chuāngtái shang yǎng le yì pén lánhuā.
example.english: She keeps a pot of orchids on the windowsill.
example.fact: 兰 is one of the 四君子 (four gentlemen) with plum, bamboo and chrysanthemum, all symbols of a refined person; orchids stand for modest elegance. It also appears in 荷兰 (the Netherlands), 兰州 and 爱尔兰 (Ireland).

examples.hanzi: 兰花在春天开放。
examples.pinyin: Lánhuā zài chūntiān kāifàng.
examples.english: Orchids bloom in spring.

examples.hanzi: 她的名字里有一个"兰"字。
examples.pinyin: Tā de míngzi lǐ yǒu yí gè "lán" zì.
examples.english: Her name has the character "兰" in it.

components.note: 石 (stone) — a rock 口 at the foot of a cliff 厂; as a radical it marks stones and minerals, as in 破, 码, 砖, 磨.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, lùshang yǒu shítou.
example.english: Careful, there is a stone on the road.
example.fact: 头 as a noun suffix turns a plain root into an everyday, concrete word — 石头 ("stone"), 木头 ("wood"), 骨头 ("bone") — a pattern that leans toward materials and substances, in contrast to the suffix 子 (as in 孩子), which leans toward living or countable things.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在河边捡石头。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài hébiān jiǎn shítou.
examples.english: The kids are picking up stones by the river.

examples.hanzi: 这座桥是用石头造的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo shì yòng shítou zào de.
examples.english: This bridge is built from stone.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — sound and speech: 吗, 叫, 喊; 响 is a sound or echo.
向 (xiàng) matches the sound except tone; also in 饷 xiǎng.

example.pinyin: Diànhuà xiǎng le.
example.english: The phone rang.
example.fact: 响 is the verb for things that make a noise, such as phones, alarms and thunder: 手机响了, 雷声很响. It also forms 响亮 (loud and clear) and 影响 (influence, which literally means shadow and echo).

examples.hanzi: 他讲话的声音很响。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎnghuà de shēngyīn hěn xiǎng.
examples.english: His speaking voice is loud.

examples.hanzi: 外面响起了雷声。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn xiǎng qǐ le léishēng.
examples.english: Thunder sounded outside.

meanings: foot (unit of length equal to 0.3048 m)

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
尸 (body) — the top part: a person. Dictionary: a man measuring by pacing; with the stroke below it, the stride or a ruler.
乚 (hook) — the bottom stroke, the measuring step. Memory aid: a foot-length ruler, as in 英尺 foot (unit).

example.hanzi: 这个房间大约有十英尺长。
example.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān dàyuē yǒu shí yīngchǐ cháng.
example.english: This room is about ten feet long.
example.fact: 英尺 literally reads "English chi" — 英 marks "English/British" the same way it does in 英里 ("mile") and 英镑 ("pound sterling"), repurposing 尺 (a traditional Chinese unit close to a third of a meter) to gloss a foreign measurement instead of coining an entirely new word.

examples.hanzi: 他身高六英尺,是个高个子。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēngāo liù yīngchǐ, shì ge gāogèzi.
examples.english: He's six feet tall, a tall guy.

examples.hanzi: 这块地宽五十英尺。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài dì kuān wǔshí yīngchǐ.
examples.english: This plot of land is fifty feet wide.

components.note: 尸 (roof, body) — 尸 acts as a roof or shelter here, as in 居 and 层; 屋 is a covered place.
至 (arrive) — 至 is where one arrives, so 屋 is a place you get to and stay — a room or house.

example.pinyin: Wūzi lǐ hěn nuǎnhuo.
example.english: It's warm in the room.
example.fact: 屋 is a bound form: spoken Chinese says 屋子 (room, especially in the north, where 里屋 means the inner room) or 房子 (house). 屋顶 is the roof, and the proverb 屋漏偏逢连夜雨 means that troubles come in clusters.

examples.hanzi: 我们的屋子在二楼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de wūzi zài èr lóu.
examples.english: Our room is on the second floor.

examples.hanzi: 外面很冷，快进屋吧。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, kuài jìn wū ba.
examples.english: It's cold outside; come in quickly.

components.note: 目 (eye) — eye above little 少: 省 is looking carefully, then saving and omitting; it is also a province, as in 省钱 save money.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shěng diǎn qián.
example.english: I want to save a little money.
example.fact: 省 is shěng for saving (省钱, 省时间) and for a province (广东省), but xǐng in 反省 (to reflect on oneself). 省略 means to omit and 省事 means labour-saving.

examples.hanzi: 他每个月省下五百块钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi gè yuè shěng xià wǔbǎi kuài qián.
examples.english: He saves five hundred yuan every month.

examples.hanzi: 山东是中国的一个省。
examples.pinyin: Shāndōng shì Zhōngguó de yí gè shěng.
examples.english: Shandong is a province of China.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸; thread is the classic fine thing, so 细 means thin, slender, then detailed — as in 线 line, 红 red.
艹 stands in for 竹 (bamboo) in the traditional 節, bamboo joints: sections, then festivals and knots.

example.hanzi: 他向我们说明了计划的细节。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒmen shuōmíng le jìhuà de xìjié.
example.english: He explained the details of the plan to us.
example.fact: 细 ("fine, thin") plus 节 ("a joint or segment," as in a bamboo stalk or 春节) combine almost literally into "a fine segment" — one small individual unit that makes up a larger whole, which is how 细节 came to mean "detail."

examples.hanzi: 这件事的细节我还不太清楚。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì de xìjié wǒ hái bú tài qīngchu.
examples.english: I'm still not clear on the details of this matter.

examples.hanzi: 做菜时,小细节很重要。
examples.pinyin: Zuò cài shí, xiǎo xìjié hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Small details matter when cooking.

components.note: 页 (head) — marks the head and face, as in 题, 额, 顺; 顶 is the top of the head, hence any top.
丁 (dīng) hints at the sound: 顶 dǐng is close to 订 dìng and 钉 dīng.

example.pinyin: Shāndǐng shang hěn lěng.
example.english: It is cold on the mountain top.
example.fact: 顶 is both the highest point (山顶, 屋顶) and a measure word for hats and tents: 一顶帽子. As a verb it means to prop, to push against, or to talk back: 顶嘴.

examples.hanzi: 我们爬到了山顶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen pá dào le shāndǐng.
examples.english: We climbed to the top of the mountain.

examples.hanzi: 他的头顶有一块小疤。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tóudǐng yǒu yí kuài xiǎo bā.
examples.english: He has a small scar on the top of his head.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 科 first meant grading grain with a measure 斗, and then categories like 科学.
斗 (dipper) — 斗 is a measuring dipper, as in 斗 (a unit of grain).
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 科学的发展改变了我们的生活。
example.pinyin: Kēxué de fāzhǎn gǎibiàn le wǒmen de shēnghuó.
example.english: The development of science has changed our lives.
example.fact: 科学 is one of many modern Chinese abstract terms borrowed back from Japanese: 19th-century Japanese scholars coined 科学 (kagaku, "branch of study") from the same characters to translate Western "science," and it was then re-imported into Chinese — the same path taken by 社会 ("society") and 经济 ("economy").

examples.hanzi: 我对科学很感兴趣,尤其是物理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì kēxué hěn gǎn xìngqù, yóuqí shì wùlǐ.
examples.english: I'm very interested in science, especially physics.

examples.hanzi: 这个说法不太科学。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shuōfǎ bú tài kēxué.
examples.english: This claim isn't very scientific.
